correctness.rationale: An Artin–Schreier reduced function with pole orders 1 and 2 defines a geometrically integral genus-six curve and two totally ramified rational poles. Exhaustive finite-field trace enumeration at extension degrees one through six yields exact point counts [2,2,77,602,3022,16337]; direct additive polynomial fiber counts cross-check degrees at most three. Newton identities plus functional equation fix the complete polynomial. An explicit Rabin irreducibility certificate in F3[T] uses exponents 12,6,4. Its Newton hull yields precisely four slopes each of 0,1/2,1. The packaged pure-Python verifier ran to VERIFY_OK. Limits: simplicity only over F5, not absolute simplicity.

value.rationale: The exact arithmetic is for the distinguished sharp-boundary genus-six positive-p-rank curve with the smallest possible full geometric automorphism group. The originating paper asks which Newton polygons coexist with that condition, so the mixed-slope example directly serves a stated mathematical question. Its irreducible degree-twelve Frobenius polynomial and F5-simplicity refine known automorphism and p-rank data rather than computing an arbitrary unmotivated coefficient. The claim is one explicit example and does not solve the general prescription problem.
